To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strategic environmental assessment (SEA) of the mainstream dams in the Mekong River Basin has been a political process in which scientific assessment played a key role in opening the discussion on the dams to a wider audience.

the environmental assessment of the Mekong dams was used by the Mekong River Commissions as a tool to open the debate on hydropower development, and that the environmental assessment process itself was used by the member countries as a means to negotiate the political terms of cooperation.
the environmental impact assessment of the twelve mainstream dams in the Mekong was designed as a political process to legitimize a pre-existing decision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how science and scientific assessment can be used in a politically sensitive and highly contested transboundary context.
the political use of scientific assessment in a context of rapid development.
the political and institutional context of environmental impact assessment in the Mekong River basin and the role of the Mekong Commission in shaping the hydropower debate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
scientific assessment in the Mekong is a narrow path between the conflicting interests of the Mekong’s riparian countries, and the worldviews that shape the debate.
the strategic environmental assessment was used to legitimize a political decision, and that it did not lead to a change in the development plans.

science-based environmental impact assessments can be used to shape governance alliances and democratize decision-making, but that this requires a political space that is not always available in the Mekong context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scientific assessment is not a tool that can be used to make decisions, but rather to make them more legitimate.
scientific assessment can provide a space for the public, NGOs and other actors to influence decision making.
scientific assessment is an important tool in the hands of the Mekong Commission to shape the debate on the future of the Mekong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mekong River is a complex system, and the scientific assessment process must be equally complex to capture its complexity.
environmental assessments can be a useful tool to promote a more open dialogue on hydropower development, and to build trust and cooperation between stakeholders.
scientific assessment is a political act, and that scientists have a responsibility to understand the political context in which they operate.
